text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
BURSA
- The Romanian Industry Ministry backs the investment of Italy's Fiat New Holland farming machinery maker in Romania's Semanatoarea.
- The upper house, the Senate, postponed debates on a local investors' bill until parliament's new session in autumn.
- The finance ministry will revise the 1997 state budget by mid-July.
ADEVARUL
- The Council of Europe's Development Fund will finance the construction of 1,300 low-cost houses in Romania. The fund will contribute 40 percent of the total cost worth $16.8 million.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- Mircea Filipoiu, head of the Romanian Commodity Exchange, said forward and futures transactions should become current in the Romanian economy. Twenty commodity exchanges opened in Romania since 1992 should find clients and develop.
- The level of cuts in profit and wage taxes will depend on budget resources and the results of talks with the IMF mission this month, said Finance Minister Mircea Ciumara.
General:
All newspapers report on the NATO summit opening in Madrid on Tuesday.
ADEVARUL
- Monthly wages of Romania's 4,000 magistrates tare o rise soon to up to 1.5 million lei, Justice Minister Valeriu Stoica said.
- The Senate ratified the Romanian-Ukrainian treaty.
- The newspaper publishes a report on prostitutes in the capital's luxury hotels.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Police in the western town of Arad, close to the border with Hungary, found five kg of heroin hidden in leather jackets.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The Senate asked a joint session to be held on Friday during which U.S. President Bill Clinton will be invited to adress Romania's parliament.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- The newspaper quotes a NATO confidential study alleging that from the military point of view, Poland and Romania should be included into the Alliance, while the Czech Republic and Hungary were militarily not prepared.

- Former prime minister Nicolae Vacaroiu said his leftist Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) would back a minority government of the National Peasant Party if it "produces good laws and renounces its ideas of restoring pre-war property and institutions."
- Dust pollution in Bucharest is 50 percent beyond the normal limits, said a report by the capital's sanitary watchdog. ($=7,103 lei)
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
